title: Operationalizing 'Responsible Scaling' Policies: A Structured Comparison

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: quantitative comparison of RSP specificity directly informs policymakers designing enforceable standards. Exposes vagueness in current commitments.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: document parsing and specificity scoring are accessible Python tasks. The policy documents are public and the analysis is largely text-based.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: collecting all public RSPs, designing a parser for varied document formats, computing specificity scores, and cross-lab comparison. Feasible but fills 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple organizations have already performed structured comparisons of responsible scaling policies. IAPS published 'Responsible Scaling: Comparing Government Guidance and Company Policy.' Enkrypt AI provides a comprehensive comparison of frontier safety frameworks. METR published 'Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies' (December 2025 update) systematically comparing policy elements across labs. The Federation of American Scientists published 'Can Preparedness Frameworks Pull Their Weight?' analyzing RSP specificity. AI Lab Watch maintains a resource tracking RSPs. The Montreal AI Ethics Institute compared OpenAI and Anthropic's governance approaches. The core contribution — structured quantitative comparison of RSP specificity — is substantially covered by this existing body of work.
